selection_reasoning: These two tasks form a natural multi-hop chain. The agent must first locate the acacia sapling in the scene, which serves as a landmark near the podzol blocks. Once the acacia sapling is found, the agent knows the general area where podzol is located and can proceed to mine it. Podzol is a dirt-variant block that requires specific tools (silk touch) or can be broken to yield dirt — the scene will provide the agent with the right tool. Both tasks are observable and verifiable: finding the sapling is visual confirmation, and mining podzol changes block state. The thematic connection is strong since podzol naturally occurs in forested biomes alongside saplings.

edges.reason: The acacia sapling serves as a visual landmark guiding the agent to the nearby podzol blocks that need to be mined

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate/observe task. The player must navigate close to the acacia sapling cluster (center sapling at spawn-relative 5,0,5, which is ~7.07 blocks from spawn) and face toward it. max_distance=5 was chosen per ValidatorAgent's recommendation — it requires the agent to walk at least ~2 blocks from spawn toward the sapling area, ensuring meaningful navigation occurred rather than triggering from spawn. facing_tolerance=60 ensures the player is actually looking at the sapling, confirming visual observation.

Uses inventory_has because mining podzol with the provided Silk Touch diamond shovel causes podzol to drop as a podzol item into the player's inventory. Without Silk Touch, podzol drops dirt instead — so this rule simultaneously verifies that (1) the agent mined a podzol block, and (2) the agent used the correct tool (the Silk Touch shovel). The player starts with zero podzol in inventory, so min_count=1 confirms successful mining. Preferred over mine_block event because inventory_has also validates the Silk Touch mechanic.
